key_insight: Reframe motion-conditioned image-to-video generation as a two-stage pipeline: first reason about plausible, causally grounded motion consequences from sparse/imprecise user trajectories, then generate the video conditioned on that reasoning—yielding more natural and consistent results.
problem_solved: User-specified motion controls (e.g., sparse trajectories) are often imprecise and causally incomplete, causing image-to-video models to produce unnatural, implausible, or missing secondary effects. MotiMotion fills in causal consequences and enforces commonsense interactions before generation.
method: Separate reasoning and generation: a visual-reasoning stage infers completed, causally consistent motion plans and secondary effects from sparse inputs.
Condition a video generator on the reasoning output to produce temporally-coherent, physically/plausibly consistent videos.
Train the reasoning module to predict commonsense causal outcomes and use its outputs to guide the generative model, improving fidelity to intended motion while filling missing details.
impact: Enables more reliable, controllable video synthesis from minimal user input, improving realism and usability for content creation, animation, and simulation tasks while reducing manual specification and post-editing.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: two-stage flow (User trajectory → Visual reasoning module → Video generator) with example intermediate outputs.
Before/after comparison: same sparse trajectory producing implausible vs. MotiMotion-corrected video frames.
Causal chain illustration: how a single input motion produces primary and secondary effects (e.g., object interactions, shadows, deformations).
Quantitative bar chart or table: improvements in realism/consistency metrics or user preference rates (visual summary of gains).
paper_title: MotiMotion: Motion-Controlled Video Generation with Visual Reasoning
paper_authors: Lee Hsin-Ying, Hanwen Jiang, Yiqun Mei, Jing Shi, Ming-Hsuan Yang
